body.statement: For the dominated QMD subfamily \(\{\mathbb P_{n,\eta}:\eta\in\mathcal K\}\), determine primitive regularity under which the reduced sample-mean experiment \(\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{mean}}\) is uniformly asymptotically equivalent, in Le Cam deficiency, to a Gaussian donor-face experiment indexed by the same \(\eta=(h,b,\Omega)\). Require the common map \(\psi_n\) to satisfy \(\sup_{\eta\in\mathcal K}\|\psi_n(\eta)-\eta\|\to0\), which separately entails uniform convergence of the local score means, \((b_{j,n})_{j\in\mathcal J}\), and \(\Omega_n\) on the compact parameter set. Establish two-sided kernel approximation only for this restricted or reduced experiment, and prove expected-diameter risk transfer under a separate uniform-integrability condition on the candidate confidence kernels, including multiple-zero-label faces.
body.justification: A common parameter map and restricted regular family are necessary before Gaussian optimality can be transferred through the discontinuous active-face target map.
body.gap: Nussbaum proves global deficiency equivalence only under strong domination, smoothness, positivity, compactness, and bounded-loss structure; fourth moments for arbitrary group laws do not supply those ingredients or uniform integrability for diameter loss.
body.consumer: A solution identifies the additional design and tail conditions under which a Gaussian face-optimal rule has a defensible reduced-micro-panel analogue.
